### SetMaxResponseBodySize

Sets the largest response body the client buffers, in bytes. A response that declares or sends more fails with `fasthttp.ErrBodyTooLarge`. A client from `New`, the default client behind the package-level helpers included, starts at 100 MiB; a client built around a `fasthttp.Client`, `HostClient` or `LBClient` keeps that client's `MaxResponseBodySize`, which `fasthttp` leaves unlimited. Zero or less removes the limit. Call it before the first request: a `fasthttp.Client` gives each host the limit it has when it first serves that host. A body read through [response streaming](#response-streaming) is not buffered and not limited, which makes streaming the way to receive a larger one.

```go title="Signature"
func (c *Client) SetMaxResponseBodySize(size int) *Client
```

:::caution
`fasthttp` allocates a buffered body from the `Content-Length` or chunk size the server declares, before the body arrives. Without a limit, a server can end the process with a response of a few bytes that declares a body too large to allocate: the Go runtime reports that as a fatal error, which `recover` cannot catch. Keep a limit for servers you do not control.
:::

### Response body size, timeouts and connection caps

`Config.MaxResponseBodySize` (default 100 MiB, a negative value for none) bounds upstream response bodies to protect against memory exhaustion. A body the proxy streams, a response set to stream with `c.Response().StreamBody` or one read by a client that streams, is held to it as well, which fasthttp does not do for a stream: a body that declares more is refused before any of it is sent, and one that passes the bound without declaring its length ends the response early. A `ModifyResponse` hook that reads a streamed body into memory takes in no more than the bound: the read fails past it, and `c.Response().Body()` then holds the error's text in place of the body. The request fails with that error, unless the hook sets a response of its own after the read, as one that reads `c.Response().BodyStream()` itself can on seeing `fasthttp.ErrBodyTooLarge`. A body that is exactly the error's text cannot be told from the failure left in place, so a hook that wants a status of its own returns an error, such as `fiber.ErrRequestEntityTooLarge`. A `Config.Client` keeps the bounds of its own clients for the bodies they buffer. fasthttp applies none to a body a client streams, whatever its `MaxResponseBodySize`, and the default does not apply to a `Config.Client`, so such a body is held only to a `Config.MaxResponseBodySize` you set and is unbounded when you leave it out. `Config.MaxConnsPerHost` (default `1024`) caps concurrent connections per upstream to limit fan-out from a single hot host. `Balancer` also bounds each request with `Config.Timeout` (default one second).
